label: lem:zero_deriv_constant
title: Zero derivative implies constant
statement: Let $G : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ and satisfy $\texttt{HasDerivAt}\; G\; 0\; x$ for all $x \in (a,b)$. Then $G(x) = G(a)$ for all $x \in [a,b]$.
proof: For any $x \in [a,b]$ with $a < x$, restrict $G$ to $[a,x]$. Apply \texttt{exists\_hasDerivAt\_eq\_slope} (the Mean Value Theorem) to obtain $c \in (a,x)$ with $G'(c) = (G(x) - G(a))/(x - a)$. Since $G'(c) = 0$ by hypothesis, we get $G(x) - G(a) = 0$, i.e., $G(x) = G(a)$.
